task: Correct canonical release child transaction scope projection to use the identical generated child task as its sealed development plan.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The live bot-driven release rehearsal #372 generated U01 expected subsystem, Known Failure and guard digest from the parent task, but the child CI evaluates the different generated child task and correctly blocked due semantic scope drift.
observableOutcomes: Canonical release-unit child plan generation and subsequent child CI calculate subsystem, Negative Knowledge, Known Failure and guard digest using the identical generated child task identity.
Parent tasks without a lexical release term still project child release-infrastructure ownership when the canonical generated child task contains release unit.
Exact child CI no longer reports a false subsystem scope or guard digest disagreement when the source and materialized child plan are valid.
The existing Knowledge, Plan, Edit-Time, Incremental, Truth, Lifecycle and security gates remain authoritative and fail closed on genuine mismatches.
An isolated replacement rehearsal can exercise the entire bot-driven post-merge main CI closure without altering prior failed rehearsal state.
unresolvedRisks: Updating canonical child task semantics may affect other release manifests or successor reprojection and needs adversarial regression.
Generated child proof identities include digests of sealed plan material; a mismatched task helper must be detected before materialization.
Active old release state is STALE and must never be rewritten to fabricate recovery or bypass the failed exact child CI.
An unrelated main commit can invalidate the new exact-head repair PR and must trigger revalidation before merging.

in: Export exactly one shared canonical child-task text helper from scripts/lib/shoperation-release-unit-runtime.mjs.
Use that helper in both the child plan binder and scripts/shoperation-plan-before-code.mjs scope projection.
Add focused regression in existing release execution binding tests for lexical parent/child scope drift and digest identity.
Apply generated lifecycle closure evidence from actual exact-head CI before PR merge.
out: No application runtime, database, auth, checkout, Builder, template or storefront changes.
No mutation to original source 65e52ffd, old U01/U02/U03 receipts, or failed DEV-POST-MERGE-EXACT-MAIN-CI-E2E-V1 remote state.
No weakening of Plan, Truth, Lifecycle, security, edit-time, release risk or negative knowledge semantics.
No unverified reuse of an old failed child CI as valid proof for a new source.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This proof drives real repository branch, pull-request, CI, merge and persisted orchestration state while deliberately restricting material changes to non-product fixtures. Exact identity, fail-closed transitions and final closure therefore require the strongest practical bounded assurance.

acceptanceCriteria: Critical Plan Before Code passes before the first implementation edit; the exact intended files and affected domain authority are declared.
One canonical generated child-task text helper is reused by both child scope projection and sealed child development task identity.
Regression demonstrates that a parent task without release lexical intent produces child release-infrastructure scope and exact matching Known Failure, Negative Knowledge and digest projections.
All existing control-plane release-unit tests pass without changing expected production behavior or suppressing known failures.
Exact-head implementation CI passes Knowledge, Plan, Edit-Time, Incremental Replay, Quality, TypeScript, Build, Completion Truth, Lifecycle and security audit.
The repair PR merges on its exact green HEAD with a green follow-up main CI; closed older releases remain byte-identical.
invariants: The generated child task and task used for scope/digest calculation are text-identical.
Child task classification includes relevant release-infrastructure intent even when parent task omits its lexical trigger.
No plan scope or digest is manually overwritten to hide a mismatch.
The old closed rehearsal and newly failed STALE state are immutable from this patch.
Exact-head proof and canonical PR merge are mandatory before claiming the code fix done.
forbiddenStates: The parent task is used for child projection while a different task string is stored in its child plan.
Child projected Negative Knowledge and guard digest differ from freshly computed CI values at the same source head.
A test is weakened to skip Plan Before Code or erase an actual classification drift.
A failed child CI is reused for canonical closure or any remote state is forced to MERGED.
An implementation commit precedes a successful canonical Plan Before Code gate.

failureModes: Parent task lacks a lexical intent found in the canonical generated child task.
Task wording drifts between planning code and binder due duplicated template strings.
Child plan digest changes while binding digest or PR metadata still refers to old plan.
Scope classification widens due task intent but the negative knowledge list is not reconciled.
CI exact head differs from the source that was plan-authorized.
Existing release-unit test suite detects a changed manifest semantics or unexpected generated path.
edgeCases: Parent task is quality-fixture only; generated child task contains the words release unit.
Parent task already includes release intent; child classification remains stable.
Child release scope has only neutral test files and a generated inert quality knowledge JSON file.
One-unit and multi-unit decomposition must produce consistent task and digest.
A stale child manifest from the former source remains rejected and cannot be reclassified after the fact.
A newly discovered duplicate task string must not override the canonical helper or create a separate authority.

alternatives.summary: Derive child task text once and reuse it for both projection and binder.
alternatives.reason: A single canonical definition removes the cause of semantic intent drift while retaining the existing rule engine and digest semantics.

alternatives.summary: Rename each parent task to contain a release term to match generated child intent.
alternatives.reason: This depends on incidental source wording and leaves the canonical projection inconsistency for future release transactions.

alternatives.summary: Suppress the child subsystem scope guard when running an inert rehearsal fixture.
alternatives.reason: This weakens fail-closed safety and would allow production release misclassification to escape proof.

specialistReviews.finding: Two call sites derive different task text for a single child transaction, breaking architectural identity coherence.
specialistReviews.resolution: Expose a single pure child-task authority and use it before emitting the sealed child transaction.

specialistReviews.finding: An automatic source classification change can silently broaden a release child's required authority or negative knowledge.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve strict scope/digest gates, test exact widened projection and reject unresolved differences instead of adding exemptions.

specialistReviews.finding: The live #372 failure makes a retry unsafe while the initial child manifest is already sealed and STALE.
specialistReviews.resolution: Leave canonical remote state untouched, merge a properly gated repair, then start a distinct new source transaction.

specialistReviews.finding: The category mismatch was correctly detected at child Plan Before Code and should be prevented in the upstream plan producer.
specialistReviews.resolution: Place a regression at child-plan projection and preserve the existing Knowledge/Atlas and failure-intake feedback.

challenge.scenario: Parent task is a neutral fixture test but child task says release unit.
challenge.finding: Using parent intent projects no release subsystem while child CI projects release-infrastructure.
challenge.resolution: Compute child expected scope from the exact generated child task string before binding.

challenge.scenario: A developer changes the generated child task wording in only the child binder.
challenge.finding: Projection digests become stale even though materialized code changes are valid.
challenge.resolution: Centralize task wording in one shared pure helper referenced by both paths.

challenge.scenario: Child scope expands but its negative knowledge acknowledgements remain from the original parent.
challenge.finding: A child can incorrectly carry one approved negative rule when thirteen are applicable.
challenge.resolution: Recompute Negative Knowledge from child-classified scope with no manual exclusions.

challenge.scenario: Child manifest already sealed on a failed source attempt is replayed after the code fix.
challenge.finding: Old plan and binding hashes cannot authorize proof under a modified generator.
challenge.resolution: Do not rewrite the failed remote state; require a new authorized source and exact-head child proof.

challenge.scenario: A release unit contains a test path and an inert quality fixture rather than production code.
challenge.finding: Lexical release intent remains operationally relevant even for non-product material, and the child CI must agree.
challenge.resolution: Retain the same classifier, recording actual released subsystem instead of downgrading classification.

challenge.scenario: A helper returns an empty task or a different parent identifier from the one used to bind the child.
challenge.finding: The child plan becomes mismatched to parent identity or loses required semantic task information.
challenge.resolution: Make helper deterministic from manifest.releaseUnitId and parentPlan.taskId and regress exact output.

challenge.scenario: A green CI exists for a previous branch head but implementation changes arrive later.
challenge.finding: Evidence reuse would be stale and could hide an updated child planning regression.
challenge.resolution: Require full exact final-head CI and lifecycle proof before merge.

challenge.scenario: The fix causes Atlas or Known Failure classification drift in unrelated scripts.
challenge.finding: Scope and security authority may expand beyond the planned two canonical scripts and one test.
challenge.resolution: Stop on any new scope blocker and re-plan before additional edits; do not suppress rules.

proofPlan: Commit plan-only critical envelope and obtain exact-head Plan Before Code PASS before writing implementation.
Review Knowledge Guard evidence, known-failure directives and the existing binder/planner source.
Add the shared child task helper and switch planner scope derivation and binder to the same authority.
Add a regression proving lexical parent/child scope consistency and digest alignment.
Run Edit-Time/Knowledge/Incremental and all exact-head PR gate checks; repair only actual failures.
Apply the CI-generated lifecycle closed plan on the authoritative head and rerun full CI.
Merge only if exact-head checks and GitHub protection rules PASS; verify merged main SHA and CI.
Keep old and failed rehearsal state unchanged; start a separate new E2E transaction only after code proof.

requirements.requirement: Child release task text must be identical for planning semantic scope projection and bound implementation transaction.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Parent task lexical scope must not replace the actual canonical child task classification.

requirements.requirement: Known Failure and Negative Knowledge projection must be derived from the generated child release subsystem scope.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Expected child negative rules and guard digest may not be silently suppressed or downgraded.

requirements.requirement: The scoped repair must achieve exact-head Truth and Lifecycle closure before merging to main.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Blocked CI or unresolved canonical state cannot be presented as completed.

notes: Plan-only issue #1170 hardening. Live #372/child #9282 demonstrated a true canonical intent scope mismatch (expected [], actual release-infrastructure, guard drift aa79c504 vs a41cfd0c). The old failed state stays STALE and source identities remain immutable. This plan is an executable authority only after PROVE_PLAN PASS; no implementation code edits before it. Recompute scope from generated child task in planner and binder, not parent task. Full Known Failure replay required for shoperation infrastructure files.
